steps.message:
## Root cause

`DocumentEditFragment.onResume()` unconditionally re-assigned the editor's text:

```java
public void onResume() {
    super.onResume();
    checkReloadDisk();
    _hlEditor.setText(_document.getContent());   // <-- resets selection to 0
}
```

`TextView.setText()` discards the current selection and places the cursor at offset 0. Since `onResume()` runs every time the app comes back to the foreground (app switch, or returning from the file-picker used by the insert-image/insert-link dialog), the cursor was silently thrown back to the start of the document. That also explains the second symptom: the insert-image dialog inserts at `_hlEditor.getSelectionStart()` when OK is pressed, so after an app switch the image landed at the beginning of the file.

The `setText` call was also redundant — `checkReloadDisk()` already reloads the document (via `loadDocumentIntoUi()`) when the file changed on disk, and `onPause()` keeps `_document` in sync with the editor content.

## Fix (`DocumentEditFragment.java`)

1. **Removed the unconditional `setText()` from `onResume()`** — the actual defect. Content refresh is left to `checkReloadDisk()`, which only reloads when the file really changed.
2. **`loadDocumentIntoUi()` now only calls `setText()` when the content actually differs** from what's in the editor, so the reload path no longer needlessly drops cursor/scroll position; the cursor is then restored through a new helper.
3. **Added `setEditorCursorPosition(int)`** which clamps the position into `[0, length]`. This also fixes an off-by-one in the old code (`_hlEditor.length() - 1`, which placed the cursor one character before the end, and `-1` on an empty document).
4. **Persist/restore the cursor position via `SAVESTATE_CURSOR_POS`** in `onSaveInstanceState()`/`onViewCreated()`, so the position also survives view re-creation (rotation, low-memory process restart).

## Verification

`./gradlew clean assembleDebug` cannot run in this environment: the build script pins Android Gradle Plugin 3.0.1 from jcenter/google, neither of which is cached locally, and network access is closed — the build fails at buildscript dependency resolution before any compilation, identically on the unmodified tree.

To confirm the change compiles, I type-checked the sources directly with `javac` against `android-27/android.jar`, the cached support-library/ButterKnife 8.8.1/lifecycle artifacts, and generated `R`/`BuildConfig` plus stubs for the non-cached third-party libs. `DocumentEditFragment.java` and all of its transitive project dependencies compile with **zero errors**, and a per-file pass over the whole `app/src/main/java` tree reports no errors either.
